sandbox.name: Docker Sandboxes
sandbox.what_it_is: MicroVM sandboxes for running coding agents
sandbox.verdict: Where people run Claude Code and Codex in yolo mode, inside a microVM rather than a container. Praised for solid isolation; knocked for workflow friction and closed source.
sandbox.notes: Counts are over 13 unique comment ids (5 ask_hn/hn_comment duplicates collapsed). False: 48458652 and 50343317 describe generic Docker containers in the authors' own projects. warpspin (50370525) liked it but distrusts Docker on security.

sandbox.name: bubblewrap
sandbox.what_it_is: Linux namespace sandbox for agent processes
sandbox.verdict: The DIY pick on Linux: people wrap Claude Code, Codex and Pi in bwrap scripts the harness cannot disable. Main knock: Linux only, and weaker than a microVM.
sandbox.notes: 14 unique ids (5 duplicates collapsed). Claude Code itself uses bwrap for its built-in sandbox (50379187).

sandbox.name: OpenShell
sandbox.what_it_is: NVIDIA policy-controlled runtime for agent fleets
sandbox.verdict: NVIDIA's policy layer for agent fleets, used by some teams to run Claude Code under granular permissions. Sceptics call it overcomplicated next to bwrap or plain Docker.
sandbox.notes: 12 unique ids (2 duplicates collapsed). Split opinion. Other points: no microVM support on Windows (50374090), telemetry that must be switched off (50200078), scepticism about the 'safe, private' naming (50199960).

sandbox.name: Apple container
sandbox.what_it_is: Apple's lightweight Linux VM containers for macOS
sandbox.verdict: Mac users build agent sandboxes on it because each container is a lightweight Linux VM. Still called a work in progress, needs macOS 26, and you must block network access yourself.
sandbox.notes: 13 unique ids. False: 49426932 is about EU packaging law for apple containers. Most mentions are as a backend option inside other tools rather than direct use.

sandbox.name: Dev containers
sandbox.what_it_is: Open spec for containerised development environments
sandbox.verdict: The no-new-tool answer: run the agent inside the devcontainer you already have. Protects against agent stupidity, not malice, and locking down the network takes real customisation.
sandbox.notes: 16 unique ids (2 duplicates collapsed). False: 49242612 is a hand-rolled podman script loosely called a devcontainer. Usage spans VS Code, Zed remote, and Kubernetes-hosted devcontainers.

sandbox.name: E2B
sandbox.what_it_is: Hosted Firecracker sandboxes for agent code execution
sandbox.verdict: The hosted sandbox people build products on: per-session agent runs, untrusted code and preview environments. Volumes get praise; the cost is platform lock-in and limited customisation.
sandbox.notes: 12 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). Positive mentions are mostly builders describing their own stacks; it is also used as the harness sandbox for Terminal-Bench runs (49825121).

sandbox.name: nono
sandbox.what_it_is: Kernel-enforced Landlock/Seatbelt sandbox for coding agents
sandbox.verdict: Runs agents under Landlock or Seatbelt without a VM, so installed tooling still works, and can inject phantom credentials. Liked, but policy config is fiddlier than Anthropic's srt.
sandbox.notes: 9 unique ids (3 duplicates collapsed). Includes the creator's own intro (47237328), counted neutral. Outside this file, warpspin (50370525, in Docker Sandboxes evidence) found it cumbersome because changes need a full restart.

sandbox.name: smolvm
sandbox.what_it_is: Lightweight cross-platform microVMs for agent sandboxing
sandbox.verdict: Where users land after trying containers and OS sandboxes; praised as light and solid enough to build a whole agent harness on. Some fear a YC rug pull.
sandbox.notes: 12 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). Three neutral mentions are from the author (binsquare). Note the top_hn_story links CelestoAI/SmolVM, a different project from smol-machines/smolvm.

sandbox.name: yoloai
sandbox.what_it_is: Agent sandbox with copy-and-diff apply workflow
sandbox.verdict: Copies your workdir into a sandbox, hides API keys, and shows a diff before changes land. Most HN mentions come from its author; one tester calls the workflow not yet smooth.
sandbox.notes: 13 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). 10 of 13 are from the author kstenerud and counted neutral as self-promotion. Thin independent signal.

sandbox.name: Daytona
sandbox.what_it_is: Hosted sandbox infrastructure for AI agents
sandbox.verdict: Mostly named in lists of hosted agent sandboxes alongside E2B and Modal, and used as interchangeable infra in experiments. The one hands-on complaint: credits are near useless until higher usage tiers.
sandbox.notes: Thin evidence. 5 false matches (Dodge Charger Daytona, Rolex Daytona, Daytona USA game, a race track, Jackie Daytona). The top_hn_story is the Dodge car, not this product.

sandbox.name: Ardent
sandbox.verdict: Gives each agent run its own copy-on-write Postgres clone so a bad query cannot touch production. HN evidence is only the founder's own posts, so there is no independent user signal yet.
sandbox.notes: 12 of 15 are false matches on the adjective 'ardent'. The 3 real ones are from founder vc289. Verdict leans on the Launch HN title and his description.

sandbox.name: Lume
sandbox.what_it_is: macOS and Linux VM CLI for Apple Silicon
sandbox.verdict: A macOS and Linux VM manager on Apple's Virtualization framework, used to sandbox Claude or run macOS-only agents. Users call it reasonably good but report setup hoops and disk resizing glitches.
sandbox.notes: 8 of 12 comments are from the Cua team (frabonacci), counted neutral. Only two independent user reports, both mixed.

sandbox.name: container-use
sandbox.what_it_is: Dagger's containerised environments for coding agents
sandbox.verdict: Dagger's tool for giving each coding agent its own container environment. The one real HN comment objects that it requires docker group access by default.
sandbox.notes: 11 of 12 are false matches on the phrase 'container use(d)'. Verdict is mostly from the tool's evident purpose (Show HN: Container Use for Agents).

local.name: Ollama
local.what_it_is: Local model runner with paid cloud tier
local.verdict: The easy path to local Qwen and Gemma, and increasingly a paid cloud plan for hosted open models like DeepSeek Flash and GLM. Few complaints beyond local models feeling limited.
local.notes: 20 unique ids (6 duplicates collapsed). 50380057 says 'ollama.cpp', ambiguous, counted neutral. Criticism appears in other tools' evidence rather than here: a user spooked by Ollama monetising moved to llama.cpp (45806027), and a 'friends don't let friends use ollama' article pushed another to llama-swap (49275239).

local.name: llama.cpp
local.verdict: A single fast binary that people move to from Ollama for control, usually serving models via llama-server. Complaints are about ROCm build friction and new flags that can cut speed.
local.notes: 23 unique ids (3 duplicates collapsed). Many neutral mentions are technical asides (MoE offload flags, quant questions). The neg is the --moe-cache-mib flag cutting throughput to a third (50377358).

local.name: MLX
local.what_it_is: Apple's array framework for Apple Silicon ML
local.verdict: The Apple Silicon route to local inference, via MLX-Serve, LM Studio or custom engines. Praised for speed with less heat than a GPU box; some still prefer llama-server on Mac.
local.notes: 18 unique ids (4 duplicates collapsed). No false matches found; all mentions are the Apple framework or its model exports.

local.name: vLLM
local.what_it_is: High-throughput GPU inference and serving engine
local.verdict: The pick for batching and throughput on dedicated GPUs, run stock by self-hosters with multi-GPU rigs. Seen as harder to deploy than llama.cpp, with reports of engine bugs on long contexts.
local.notes: 17 unique ids. Four neutral entries are Who's Hiring CV lines listing vLLM as a skill.

local.name: Open WebUI
local.what_it_is: Self-hosted chat UI for local and API models
local.verdict: The usual self-hosted chat front end over Ollama, llama.cpp or APIs, extended with plugins and Open Terminal. Feature-rich, but wiring up tools like search is painful and setup feels heavy.
local.notes: 23 unique ids (3 duplicates collapsed). The notes feature gets specific praise (48417329). One older user dismissed it as just an Ollama front end (45806027).

local.name: LM Studio
local.what_it_is: Desktop GUI app for running local models
local.verdict: The GUI on-ramp for local models, often paired with Aider, Continue or Cline and praised for easy setup and model switching. Newer gripe: it now steers downloads to its agentic app.
local.notes: 25 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). Several neutral entries are quoted questions or screenshots. Context-window complaints (45778334) are mostly about hardware limits. Unsloth Desktop is mentioned as a strong alternative (50242615).

local.name: Unsloth
local.what_it_is: Quantized model builds, fine-tuning and desktop app
local.verdict: Best known as the source of quantized GGUFs people actually run, with even IQ1 DeepSeek quants holding up. Unsloth Desktop is gaining fans; complaints are tight context limits and no VRAM-to-RAM splitting.
local.notes: 15 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). Most neutral mentions are file paths or benchmarks naming an Unsloth quant. Desktop praise also appears in LM Studio evidence (50242615).

local.name: Lemonade
local.what_it_is: AMD's local LLM server for GPU and NPU
local.verdict: AMD's all-in-one local server and the go-to on Strix Halo, with easy installers and one endpoint for chat, images and speech. Owners say it replaced most cloud use; one reports weaker speeds.
local.notes: False: 50158123 is the 'make lemonade' idiom. Strong positive sentiment from Strix Halo owners.

local.name: SGLang
local.what_it_is: High-performance LLM serving framework for GPU clusters
local.verdict: A datacenter serving engine named alongside vLLM for multi-GPU inference. Recent talk centres on a Cloudflare KV-cache leak involving an SGLang state bug, though some put the blame on Cloudflare's config.
local.notes: Negative count is driven by one incident thread (Cloudflare GLM-5.3 Workers AI leak). Three neutral entries are CV lines. Little hands-on user discussion.

local.name: llama-swap
local.what_it_is: Model-swapping proxy in front of llama-server
local.verdict: The proxy home-lab users put in front of llama.cpp to hot-swap models behind one OpenAI-style endpoint. Called bulletproof by fans; critics say it adds hard-to-debug complexity now llama-server can juggle models itself.
local.notes: Often paired with bifrost or OpenRouter fallback. Docs criticised as little more than a sample config (49275520).

local.name: Apfel
local.what_it_is: CLI and API for Apple's on-device model
local.verdict: Wraps Apple's on-device Foundation Model as a CLI and OpenAI-style server, so the Mac's built-in model answers quick shell questions. Liked as useful; Apple's own first-party server may now overlap it.
local.notes: Three neutral entries are from the maintainer (franze). Small but uniformly positive signal; one user says it tempts them to upgrade to Tahoe (48457423).

local.name: KoboldCpp
local.what_it_is: Single-file llama.cpp runner with built-in UI
local.verdict: One executable bundling llama.cpp with a web UI, image generation and speech, favoured by roleplay users for its tunables. Praised for zero-install simplicity, if a bit jack of all trades.
local.notes: Several neutral entries are technical asides (RNG seeds, Krea2 support). Roleplay preference comes from the AI Horde comment (48878731).

local.name: Jan
local.what_it_is: Open-source desktop chat app for local models
local.verdict: The open-source desktop alternative to LM Studio: a simple chat window that searches and downloads GGUF models with no lock-in. Often recommended as an easy start; the threads hold no real complaints.
local.notes: Mentions are mostly short recommendations in 'alternatives to Ollama/LM Studio' threads; little depth.

gateways.name: OpenRouter
gateways.what_it_is: Pay-as-you-go API router across model providers
gateways.verdict: The pay-as-you-go side door to open-weight models like DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi, used to test models, run side projects and get past refusals. Main gripe: frontier models cost more there than subscriptions.
gateways.notes: 26 unique ids. Also used to trial open models before buying local hardware (50398416).

gateways.name: LiteLLM
gateways.what_it_is: Python SDK and proxy unifying LLM APIs
gateways.verdict: The common self-hosted gateway that teams point tools at for cheap multi-model access and token metering. Talk now centres on its PyPI supply-chain compromise and whether it can be trusted.
gateways.notes: 14 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). Four neutral entries are CV or job-post stack lines. Outside this file, a Portkey user calls LiteLLM's proxy code slow and messy (47506280).

gateways.name: AWS Bedrock
gateways.what_it_is: AWS managed API for Claude and other models
gateways.verdict: How companies buy Claude and other models at work: API pricing, budgets tracked with AWS spend, stronger privacy guarantees. Works well, but it costs more than Anthropic's own subscriptions.
gateways.notes: 14 unique ids (4 duplicates collapsed). Several neutral entries are CVs and job posts. No figurative 'bedrock' false matches in this set.

gateways.name: OpenCode Go / Zen
gateways.what_it_is: OpenCode's subscription and pay-per-use model access
gateways.verdict: The budget pick: $10 a month buys generous open-weight usage, mostly DeepSeek Flash, and users rarely hit limits. The one knock is free Zen models rotating into the paid tier.
gateways.notes: Strongly positive. Zero-retention claim noted (48740921). One user stacks five accounts (50375807).

gateways.name: llm (Simon Willison)
gateways.what_it_is: CLI and Python library for many LLMs
gateways.verdict: Simon Willison's CLI and Python library for prompting any model through plugins, with exportable logs. Others build plugins and IPython tools on it and praise its docs; core releases have slowed.
gateways.notes: 8 false matches on generic 'LLM tools'. All 7 neutral entries are simonw describing his own tool. 'Core releases have slowed' rests on his Dec 2025 comment (46254305).

gateways.name: Claude Code Router
gateways.what_it_is: Proxy routing Claude Code to other models
gateways.verdict: The usual way to keep Claude Code's harness while swapping in Kimi, Grok, DeepSeek or local Qwen, handy when quota runs out. One user found tool-call translation never fully lined up.
gateways.notes: Most evidence is from early 2026. 47918768 is about a repackaged copy of the tool, counted neutral.

gateways.name: Vercel AI Gateway
gateways.what_it_is: Vercel's hosted multi-provider model API gateway
gateways.verdict: Shows up mainly as where new models launch, sometimes free, and as a pay-per-token work account. Gripes: a required credit card, and third-party routing with the usual provider quality issues.
gateways.notes: 12 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). Several neutral entries are vendor launch posts (Boundless, Pixel Canary, Jev).

gateways.name: cc-switch
gateways.what_it_is: Provider switcher for Claude Code and Codex
gateways.verdict: A switcher that points Claude Code or Codex at cheaper models like MiniMax or DeepSeek, translating between API formats. Thin evidence, but the users who mention it are happy.
gateways.notes: Only 3 unique comments (1 duplicate collapsed). 49343556 reads somewhat promotional.

gateways.name: Chutes
gateways.what_it_is: Decentralised GPU inference with TEE-served models
gateways.verdict: Cheap open-model inference from trusted execution environments, so GPU owners cannot read prompts. One newcomer found no documented route into OpenCode or Claude Code.
gateways.notes: 13 unique ids (1 duplicate collapsed). 5 false matches (parachutes, laundry chutes, etc.). Privacy guarantees questioned as not strong enough (49535073).

gateways.name: Portkey
gateways.what_it_is: Hosted AI gateway with routing and logging
gateways.verdict: An AI gateway that shows up in benchmark comparisons against LiteLLM and Bifrost. The one hands-on report switched from LiteLLM's proxy on the free plan and found it much faster.
gateways.notes: Thin evidence, 5 comments. False: 47820031 is the Harry Potter portkey.

gateways.name: OmniRoute
gateways.what_it_is: Self-hosted local router for model providers
gateways.verdict: A self-hosted router for model APIs, named once as someone's local counterpart to OpenRouter. Too little HN discussion to judge it.
gateways.notes: Single comment. It links diegosouzapw/OmniRoute while the tool url is cheaper-inference/OmniRoute; worth checking they are the same project.

gateways.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
gateways.what_it_is: Cloudflare proxy for LLM calls with spend controls
gateways.verdict: A proxy in front of model APIs for monitoring, caching and spend caps without hosting your own. Complaints: budgets are fixed-window rules and reported prices can be wrong.
gateways.notes: False: 47397044 does not mention the gateway. Two neutral entries are from Cloudflare's kentonv.

gateways.name: Synthetic
gateways.verdict: A flat subscription for open-weight models such as DeepSeek Flash, pitched at OpenCode users. The only HN mention is from a cofounder, so there is no independent signal.
gateways.notes: Single comment from cofounder reissbaker. Verdict leans on the tool's evident purpose and top story title.
